analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses against the replayed patches, metadata, changelog and canonical threat index, including T-041's detailed cache contract. No independently supported security regression is visible. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md:3,702 changes a date and GatedDelta source reference, not the documented probe or memory policy. provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/BackendParityHarness.swift:435 qualifies the assistant loader with MLXLLM while retaining the target check and drafter construction; the patch alone establishes no validation bypass. Neither change visibly alters authorization, token custody, hop encryption, billing or privileged fan authority.
The combined material change is the native dependency advance at libs/mlx:1, libs/mlx-swift:1 and libs/mlx-swift-lm:1. changelog.d/mlx-upstream-sync-2026-10-22.md:3–5 describes nested dependency updates, changed Metal kernels and SDK adaptations, but supplies no implementation proof. Review remains necessary for TB-007/A-001: kernel bounds and numerical equivalence, request-state/PrefillParameters isolation, cancellation (T-010), residual memory (T-028), image/video .source handling (T-050), and throwing weight-sanitization cleanup. Verify relocated GatedDelta probing and preservation of T-041's authenticated cache scope, model/layout bindings, encrypted SSD policy and staging reservations. Changed metallib/artifacts also require checking the existing exact-artifact qualification contract (A-017/T-054); no qualification bypass is demonstrated here.
Replay omits five source units, including the configuration excerpt discussed by the prior analysis; its claimed date/row-only edits cannot be independently rechecked here. The prior questions about provider adaptations and assistant-loading behavior remain unresolved because their implementations and dependency deltas are absent. Further review of those changed implementations is warranted, rather than treating missing evidence as a vulnerability or declaring the dependency update safe.
